official_measurement_examples.fact: Solar PV on domestic buildings can be permitted development under Part 14 where all applicable limitations and conditions are met.
A common domestic Part 14 limitation is that equipment must not protrude more than 0.2 metres beyond the plane of the wall or roof slope, subject to the exact class conditions.
Permitted development rights differ between domestic and non-domestic solar classes and must not be merged.
Where Part 14 conditions are not met, a planning application may be required; permitted development is not a universal exemption from planning control.
Listed-building consent can be separately required even where a planning permitted-development analysis appears favourable.
Conservation-area or designated-site context can change applicable limitations and must be checked against the relevant class.
A roof-solar PDR does not prove structural suitability, grid connection, electrical compliance or installation feasibility.
Solar permitted-development status does not establish ownership, roof rights, planning history clearance or final development yield.

core_rules: Part14 PDR is conditional not universal
domestic and non-domestic classes remain distinct
PDR failure can require planning permission
PDR is not listed building consent
PDR does not prove structural suitability
PDR does not prove grid capacity
PDR does not prove electrical compliance
PDR does not establish roof rights
PDR does not calculate development yield
historic PDR amendments must retain date
Article4 or condition restrictions must be checked
no parcel solar clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
